newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan current account surplus surges in January.
newsitem.headline: Japan current account surplus surges in January.

text.p: Japan's surplus in its current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, rose sharply in January, marking the first increase in 17 months, the Finance Ministry announced on Thursday.

The surplus totalled 150.7 billion yen in January, compared with a surplus of 32.6 billion yen a year earlier, exceeding economists' expectations. But the surplus in merchandise trade alone, a narrower measure of trade, fell to 229.3 billion yen from 271.3 billion yen a year earlier.
At Thursday's rate of 121 yen to the dollar, the current account surplus in January amounted to $1.24 billion, while the merchandise trade surplus was $1.89 billion.

The surge in the surplus confounded analysts' forecasts, which had ranged from a big deficit in the current account to a modest increase in the surplus. In a Reuters poll, the average of economists' forecasts had been for a deficit of 31 billion yen ($256 million).
January figures are notoriously unpredictable as the length of the New Year holiday, including weekends, varies from year to year, affecting the number of business days.

Japan's contentious current account surplus fell in December for the 16th consecutive month of year-on-year declines. But the pace of the drop had slowed due to the yen's fall in value since mid-1995, which has boosted exports while discouraging imports.
